title: Canonical coefficient comparison for the constructible tensor
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$, its coefficient datum $c$ with prime $\ell\ne p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ with geometric fibre $T$, and a finite coefficient field $E\subset c.\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $F$ be the normalized coefficient comparison system [def-fd-coefficient-comparison-datum] [def-fd-pullback-comparison-datum] and $W$ its geometric-Frobenius fixed-pair comparison [def-sf-projection-weil-coefficient-comparison]. The canonical coefficient tensor comparison identifies the coefficient image of the framework rational tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] with the ordinary rational tensor of a normalized comparison $R$ [def-sf-projection-weil-tensor-comparison]. It is defined by the following normalization. The ordinary coefficient tensor and signed-total comparison [def-sf-projection-coefficient-tensor-total] is as follows. Ordinary scalar restriction through the quotient-normalized completed ring isomorphism sends every local pure tensor $x\otimes y$ to that same tensor of the restricted sections. Sum its inverse over all bidegrees with the signed total differential, and descend the resulting comparison on flat-term K-flat representatives through the two tensor representative isomorphisms and the exact coefficient-transport factorization. The integral normalization is required for every normalized tensor-completion presentation [def-sf-tensor-completion-comparison], whose representative square fixes the quotient coordinate and zero shifted coordinate. Such presentations exist by [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion], so this normalization is nonvacuous. On integral constructible objects, first apply the inverse of the actual quotient-tower completion unit of [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion], then this ordinary derived comparison, and lift through the full integral inclusion. Finally localize this uniquely prescribed integral comparison on every unchanged integral representative, using the object and pure-tensor normalizations of $F$ and $R$. This defines a unique natural isomorphism of the two indicated rational tensor bifunctors; it retains every rational denominator and requires no integral lift of a rational Weil structure.
